subsystems.name: Light-field panel
subsystems.role: shows a dense set of views at once so several people can see 3D without glasses.

subsystems.name: Aerial voxel engine
subsystems.role: draws the floating part of the image — bright points in empty air.
parts: scanning mirrors or spatial light modulator

subsystems.name: Eye and hand tracking
subsystems.role: finds where each eye is and what the hands are doing, many times a second.

subsystems.name: Haptic layer
subsystems.role: lets the user feel invisible controls.

subsystems.name: Render and warp pipeline
subsystems.role: draws the right view for the right eye fast enough that it feels solid.

subsystems.name: Safety envelope
subsystems.role: keeps laser and ultrasound exposure inside legal limits.

buildSteps.title: Pick the image method
buildSteps.detail: Decide how much of the picture is a light-field panel and how much is drawn as points in air. Aerial voxels are the hard, bright, risky part; the panel can carry the rest.

buildSteps.title: Build the panel
buildSteps.detail: A high-resolution screen is covered with a lenslet array or given a directional backlight, so each pixel emits many narrow beams and a viewer sees a different image from each position.

buildSteps.title: Add eye tracking
buildSteps.detail: Infrared cameras watch the face and eyes; software estimates gaze in a few milliseconds. This steers extra view resolution toward each pupil instead of spreading it over all directions.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the aerial voxel engine
buildSteps.detail: A laser is focused to a tiny point; scanning mirrors sweep that point through a volume. Air plasma glows briefly at the focus, or a trapped light-absorbing particle is moved and lit. Brighter, larger volumes need faster scanning and more laser power.

buildSteps.title: Design the safety envelope
buildSteps.detail: Choose wavelengths that are strongly absorbed by water in the eye, keep scattered exposure under laser-safety limits, enclose stray beams, and interlock the laser so it stops if anything enters the volume. Ultrasound haptics must stay inside accepted exposure limits too.

buildSteps.title: Fuse tracking, haptics and interaction
buildSteps.detail: Hand and finger positions drive objects; a phased array of ultrasound emitters focuses pressure at the fingertips; clicks, drags and gestures get visual and tactile feedback.

buildSteps.title: Tune the render loop
buildSteps.detail: The GPU renders per-eye views at high frame rate and reprojects them at the last instant using fresh eye data, so head movement does not break the illusion of a solid object.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate everything
buildSteps.detail: Eye tracker, panel and laser volume are aligned into one coordinate frame and re-checked as the user moves around the desk.

buildSteps.title: Validate with users and regulators
buildSteps.detail: Depth-accuracy, comfort, fatigue and multi-user tests, plus laser and ultrasound certification, before anything can be sold.

prerequisites.why: desktop 3D panels exist, but resolution per view is far below what a full workspace needs.
plasma and trapped-particle displays have been shown in labs; they are small, dim and slow.
demonstrated in prototypes; limited force and small working volume.
shipped in headsets and phones; provides the gaze data the display needs.
GPUs can render many views per frame, which was impossible a decade ago.

pathway.milestone: eye-tracked light-field desktops and stereo AR/VR headsets
pathway.unlocks: glasses-free 3D at a desk for one or two viewers, without the floating image.

pathway.milestone: brighter, larger eye-safe aerial voxel volumes plus fused hand tracking and haptics
pathway.unlocks: reaching into a 3D scene and feeling it respond — the core of the concept.

pathway.milestone: hybrid workstations that combine a light-field panel with sparse aerial highlights
pathway.unlocks: practical desks where only the objects you touch are drawn in mid-air.

pathway.milestone: certified, full-parallax, multi-user volumetric workspaces at usable resolution and colour
pathway.unlocks: shared 3D design and control rooms replacing walls of 2D screens.
